title: Surgical failsafe orchestrator for config toggles and cost-driven tripwires
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a surgical failsafe orchestrator that applies config changes (batching / caching / quantization / routing policy tweaks) with automated tripwires tied to cost and SLA signals, plus deterministic safe revert logic and state reconciliation. Goal: reduce manual toil for safe cost-driven tuning while guaranteeing platform stability and a clear runbook for on-call engineers. This ticket scopes the controller, preflight simulation, canary shadow apply, tripwire definitions, and the reconcile/repair state machine.

Problems we are solving:
- Safety: config changes can materially increase per-token cost or regress latency SLOs. Current manual rollback is slow and error-prone.
- Observability: lack of consistent pre- and post-apply signal comparison (cost delta, P50/P95/P99 latency, error-rate, KV-hit rate).
- Reconciliation: rollbacks and partial failures leave inconsistent runtime state across pools.

High-level design decisions and rationale:
- Tripwire model: Create declarative tripwires that evaluate rolling-window deltas and absolute thresholds for cost-per-token, request-error-rate, P99 latency, and KV cache hit-rate. Tripwires are labeled as 'soft' (alert + pause rollout) or 'hard' (automatic revert). We choose dual-mode to balance sensitivity and noise.
- Canary apply pattern: Staged shadow apply -> staged canary (small fraction of live traffic served) -> progressive ramp where metrics must pass for each step. Shadow apply runs side-by-side with no egress billing to verify functional compatibility and cache warmup.
- Preflight simulation: Use historical traffic replay (sampled traces) for a dry-run cost estimate and KV-cache warmup estimate. This reduces false positives from cold-cache effects.
- Reconciliation and idempotency: Each config change is applied as a versioned intent with a snapshot of prior runtime state. Reconciler is responsible for detecting drift (partial apply, pod crashes) and performing deterministic actions: complete apply, rollback, or mark for manual review. Snapshots are stored as metadata only (keys + hashes), not full traces.
- Safety nets: Hysteresis windows, minimum stable time per stage, cooldown periods between successive rollouts. Provide manual override with escalation if automated revert would cause worse customer impact.

Acceptance criteria (must have):
- Controller can perform a shadow apply and collect pre/post metrics from sampled traces and live telemetry.
- Declarative tripwires can be configured per-project and per-model; hard tripwires auto-revert within the configured window.
- Rollback path is idempotent and leaves runtime in a reconciled state with audit log entry. No dangling partial-state across >1 node/pool after rollback.
- Dashboard with before/after cost delta, latency histograms, KV hit-rate, and triggered tripwires for each rollout.
- Runbook and PagerDuty playbook for manual escalation.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement cross-region automated failover.
- We will not change billing systems; cost signals are observational for rollback decisions.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict auto-revert vs manual review: strict auto-revert reduces blast radius but may oscillate on noisy signals. We implemented soft-vs-hard tripwires and minimum stabilization windows to mitigate oscillation risks.
- Preflight replay accuracy: replay reduces cold-cache false positives but increases complexity and requires sampled traces retention; we limit to 48-hour sampling window to bound storage and compute.
- Scope creep: We intentionally defer fine-grained per-customer quotas and legal audit hooks (for Private customers) into a follow-up.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Core controller and intent model (2 weeks): versioned intent store, apply/rollback APIs, audit events.
2) Shadow apply + telemetry collection (2 weeks): implement shadow mode, integrate with metrics pipeline and cost estimation function.
3) Tripwire engine (1 week): declarative rules, soft/hard modes, hysteresis.
4) Canary ramp and revert automation (1 week): staged traffic ramp, auto-revert logic.
5) Reconciler and repair (1 week): detect partial applies and perform deterministic repair.
6) Dashboards, runbooks, doc + security review (1 week).

Metrics and dashboards to build:
- Cost per 1k tokens delta (pre/post) with CI on difference.
- P99 latency, error rate, KV hit-rate time series per canary cohort.
- Tripwire triggers annotated on the timeline (with rule name and computed delta).

APIs and artifacts:
- Config Intent API (internal): POST /config-intents apply, GET status, POST /config-intents/:id/rollback. (proto sketch in Confluence).
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/FailSafe+Orchestrator+Design (draft).
- GitHub RFC/PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1289 (WIP).
- Dashboard prototype (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/rollback-playbook (private link).

Security and compliance:
- No secrets or customer data in snapshots. Snapshots are hashes of config and node membership. Security review required before merge.

Open questions: 
- What is the exact traffic fraction for the initial canary (suggest 1%)?
- How many retries before marking a revert as manual?
- How to handle dependent config changes that must be applied as atomic groups?

Deliverables:
- Controller implementation + unit/integration tests.
- Tripwire DSL and examples for batching/caching tuning.
- Canary pipeline and automated revert logic.
- Dashboard and runbook.

Acceptance test notes: use test cluster with synthetic traces and a standing A/B test to validate revert semantics; verify state reconciliation by killing nodes mid-apply and ensuring reconciler completes or rolls back cleanly.

2025-10-02: UX review with PMs (Eleanor Wong) — requested explicit manual-override in Console and a mandatory dry-run toggle for enterprise customers. Added to scope. — Aisha
2025-10-04: Integration test failure observed when a canary pod crashes during stage-2 ramp. Reconciler now records per-pod apply state and retries reconcile steps. — Marco
2025-10-07: Security review kickoff scheduled for 2025-10-12; confirmed snapshots contain no PII and will be hashed. — Security (Jamal).
